title: Why Is This Harp Seal the Worst Mother?
negative_prompt: people, human hands, researchers, boats, buildings, text baked into artwork, letters, logos, watermark, cartoon, anime, tears, human-like expressions, duplicate seals, extra limbs, deformed anatomy, adult saddle markings on a white-coated pup, newborn white coat on the older juvenile, fabricated rescue, mother returning after weaning, graphic drowning

worlds.base_prompt: Premium painterly natural-history illustration in vertical 9:16 composition. North Atlantic pack ice, slate-blue water, soft overcast light, cinematic depth, anatomically accurate harp seals, no people or equipment. Preserve developmental continuity: nursing pup has a white lanugo coat; later post-weaning juvenile has a gray-spotted coat. Every shot should visibly prove the narration with a materially distinct composition.

narration.narration: Why is this harp seal the worst mother? She nurses her pup for about twelve days. Then she leaves.
No more meals from Mom. And it is not ready to feed itself. So what keeps it alive?
Before leaving, her milk helps it gain about five pounds a day and build fat reserves.
That fat becomes its food supply for weeks.
But there is a catch. The pup still needs ice while its diving ability develops. If storms break it up too early, young pups can drown.
Surviving pups begin feeding for themselves.
She left it with fuel, not a guarantee. Her milk buys time. The ice has to last.

shots.transformation: Five-second restrained nursing movement: the pup shifts into contact while the mother remains calm; no morphing or size change.

evidence.claim: Harp seal pups are nursed for about 12 days; after weaning they fast on the ice before independent feeding.
evidence.qualification: Use about; do not imply every pup follows an identical schedule or that every immersion is fatal.

evidence.claim: During nursing harp seal pups gain roughly 2.2 kg, about five pounds, per day and build substantial energy reserves/blubber.
evidence.qualification: Do not imply all gained mass is pure fat; the narration says milk helps build fat reserves.

evidence.claim: Stable ice supports nursing and post-weaning resting; poor ice can break in storms and young pups can drown.
evidence.qualification: Say can, not that every pup inevitably drowns or that the illustrated pup is guaranteed to die.

evidence.claim: Surviving pups eventually enter the water and begin feeding independently.
evidence.qualification: Use surviving pups and begin; do not guarantee the outcome for a particular individual.

prohibited_claims: Do not present 'worst mother' as an objective scientific ranking or attributed public verdict.
Do not show the mother returning after weaning.
Do not imply that every young harp seal is incapable of swimming.
Do not guarantee survival or death for the illustrated pup.
Do not return the ending juvenile to newborn white-coat appearance.
